- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift mean down.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward after spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a downward bias of 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment spike, true price often reverses or drops sharply; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 10–15 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment-driven reversal or downward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true price deviates >5% from model in first 5–7 days, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows sudden spike (e.g., 1.00) followed by 0.00, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak or adjust downward after spike.
